key_insight: CREW replaces fixed multi-agent related-work pipelines with learned, dynamic collaboration among LLM agents to improve synthesis quality for automatic related work generation.
engineering_relevance: The framework is relevant for scalable scientific writing tools because it can reduce manual literature-review effort while also lowering token cost through adaptive agent coordination.
method: Agents autonomously choose actions: Retrieve, Disseminate, Compose, and Critique.
Policy is optimized with Independent Proximal Policy Optimization (IPPO).
Designed as a collaborative multi-agent RL framework rather than a rigid heuristic workflow.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments on a standard RWG benchmark, showing better quality than strong baselines and lower token costs.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on careful RL training and stable agent coordination, so results may be sensitive to benchmark setup and implementation details.
paper_title: Assembling the CREW: A Collaborative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Automated Related Work Generation
